seriesTitle: Multi-Channel Rotary Selector Valves with PEEK or PCTFE Heads
cardHeading: {0}-channel ceramic rotary selector valve for reagent selection and wash-path switching, with a {1} mm bore and {2} ports
introDefinition: FOREACH {0} is a {1}-channel ceramic rotary selector valve for integration into automated equipment. It supports reagent selection and wash-path switching in instrument fluidics and laboratory automation systems, working with a pump and the equipment control program to select reagent or wash-fluid connections in sequence.
introMaterials: The valve uses a zirconia stator and sapphire rotor, with motor-driven rotation to switch fluid paths. PEEK or PCTFE valve-head configurations allow wetted materials to be selected for the reagents, cleaning fluids and operating conditions.
introIntegration: For integration, use the flow diagram to establish connection requirements, then check bore size, port threads, internal volume and mounting requirements. Material combinations and specifications depend on the selected ordering model.
seriesDescription: FOREACH MRV3 rotary selector valves are OEM fluidic components for reagent selection and wash-path switching in analytical instruments and laboratory automation equipment. The range includes 10-, 16- and 24-channel configurations, using motor-driven rotation to select liquid connections within an automated fluidic system.
seriesIntegration: MRV3 valves use a zirconia stator and sapphire rotor, with RS232 / RS485 communication for instrument control. Availability of PEEK or PCTFE valve heads depends on the specific model. Select by the required fluidic connections, channel count, bore size, port thread and internal volume, and check wetted-material compatibility with the reagents and cleaning fluids.
seriesConfigurationLinks: Compare 10-, 16- and 24-channel configurations by the connections in your flow diagram. See [MRV3-D10]({0}{1}mrv3-d10/), [MRV3-D16]({2}{3}mrv3-d16/) and [MRV3-D24]({4}{5}mrv3-d24/) to compare bore size, internal volume and ports, and select wetted materials.
selection10: Start with this configuration when the planned reagent, wash and spare connections fit the 10-channel flow diagram. The 1.2 mm bore does not define a fixed flow rate; check the fluid, pump, pressure drop and tubing together.
selection16: Consider 16 channels when 10 cannot cover the planned connections. Ports remain 1/4-28 UNF, but the bore and internal volume change. Confirm mounting and control requirements before treating the configurations as interchangeable.
selection24: The 24-channel configuration changes both bore size and port threads. Check 6-40 UNF fittings, tubing bore and fluid condition. The 2.9 μL value is valve internal volume, not a dispensing volume or a carryover specification.
selectionSeries: Determine connection needs from the flow diagram, then compare bore size, ports, materials and internal volume. Channel count does not specify the number of independently operating simultaneous flows.
switchingValue: ≤2 s per revolution; <100 ms between adjacent ports
volumeDefinitionValue: Volume of the COM-port passage and rotor groove
faqTasksQuestion: What fluid-handling tasks can the {0} rotary selector valve perform?
faqTasksAnswer: The {0} selects fluid paths for sequential reagent access, sample collection and distribution, and switching between reagent and wash connections. It works with a pump; the instrument control program coordinates valve positions with aspiration and delivery for automated fluidic modules.
faqChannelsQuestion: When should I choose the {0}-channel configuration?
faqChannelsAnswer: Count the reagent, wash and spare connections in your flow diagram, including their relationship to the common port. The {0} has {1} channels, with a {2} mm bore and {3} ports. Match the connection count, tubing and flushing sequence to the intended system.
faqMaterialsQuestion: How do I choose between PEEK and PCTFE valve heads?
faqMaterialsAnswer: MRV3 offers PEEK and PCTFE valve-head options. Compare both reagent and cleaning-fluid composition, concentration, temperature and contact time, and include the stator, rotor and other wetted parts in the compatibility review. Provide the actual fluids and operating conditions to select the head material and ordering configuration.
faqControlQuestion: How is the rotary valve controlled, and how fast does it switch?
faqControlAnswer: MRV3 uses motor-driven switching with optical position sensing and automatic homing on power-up. It supports RS232 and RS485 communication at 9600, 57600 or 115200 baud, with switching times of ≤2 s per revolution and <100 ms between adjacent ports. The motor and driver are optional; coordinate switching with pump operation during integration.
faqWashQuestion: How should the fluid path be flushed between reagents?
faqWashAnswer: A channel can be reserved for cleaning fluid. Before changing reagents, switch to that channel and use the pump to pass cleaning fluid through the valve and connected tubing, then select the next reagent. Determine the amount of cleaning fluid and the number of flushes by testing with the actual tubing, reagents and acceptable residue level.
faqCustomQuestion: What information is needed to configure the {0}?
faqCustomAnswer: Provide the flow diagram, channel count, reagents and cleaning fluids, operating pressure and temperature, tubing and port requirements, mounting space, communication interface and switching sequence. We use these requirements to select the valve-head material, motor and driver, and confirm available combinations.
integrationAdvantage: RS232 / RS485 communication; confirm power, mounting space and pump–valve sequencing before integration.
flushingAdvantage: Use internal volume in flow-path calculations; validate flushing performance in the complete system.
applicationsIntro: {0} supports instrument workflows that need to switch automatically between liquid connections: selecting reagents, changing sample-processing steps or directing liquid to different destinations. The valve selects the connection, the pump moves the liquid, and the instrument program coordinates the sequence.
reagentContext: An analytical method may require several reagents to be added in sequence. Connect the reagent reservoirs to separate channels so the valve can select the required reagent before the pump delivers it to a reaction vessel or detection unit.
reagentBenefit: {0} provides the switching step so reagent connections can follow the analytical method. Allocate channels for both reagents and cleaning fluid; the paired pump and instrument program control the delivered volume and speed.
sampleTitle: Sample Preparation: Switching Between Sampling, Reagents and Washing
sampleContext: Before analysis, a sample-processing sequence may require sample transfer, addition of processing liquids and washing of the connected tubing. Each step uses a different liquid connection and must be coordinated with pump aspiration and delivery.
sampleBenefit: {0} can select sample, processing-liquid or wash connections in the required sequence. When samples pass through the valve, consider particles, material adhesion and the permitted residue between samples when designing the workflow.
distributionTitle: Automated Liquid Distribution: One Supply, Multiple Destinations
distributionContext: When several vessels or instrument locations use the same liquid, a distribution valve can select their supply connections in sequence. After the pump completes delivery through one channel, the valve selects the next channel for the following delivery.
distributionBenefit: {0} provides channel switching for this sequential supply arrangement. The instrument controls delivery volume, dwell time and order, while the channel count must accommodate the intended destinations and spare connections.
washContext: When different reagents pass through shared tubing, a wash step can be included between reagent changes. Connect cleaning fluid to a channel, select it after the previous reagent step and use the pump to flush the valve and tubing before selecting the next reagent.
washBenefit: Include this wash step in the automated operating sequence. Set the amount of cleaning fluid and number of flushes according to tubing length, reagent properties and acceptable residue, then check the result using the actual liquids.
needsText: Tell us which liquids the instrument uses, in what order, how many vessels or locations must be connected, and the volume and timing required at each step. Share a connection diagram, reagent and cleaning-fluid details, temperature, pressure, ports and available mounting space so we can match the channel configuration, valve-head material, motor and driver.
